info.desc: Achtung Baby is the seventh studio album by Irish rock band U2, released on 19 November 1991. The album arrived nearly two years after lead vocalist Bono announced the band would have to "go away and dream it all up again", following the mixed response to 1988's Rattle and Hum. While recording Achtung Baby, there was a rift between band members over the direction of the band's sound. podcast.body: Released on November 19, 1991, as the follow-up to "The Joshua Tree," U2 consciously sought to reinvent their sound. Early recording sessions were difficult, but moving to Berlin (around the time the Berlin Wall fell) helped the band find new influences in avant-garde electronic, industrial, dance, and alternative music. This marked a shift from their serious, politically conscious image to a more playful, self-deprecating approach. It sold an estimated 20-25 million units and is considered, along with "The Joshua Tree," to represent U2 at the peak of their powers. "they needed to reinvent themselves again."

podcast.body: The events surrounding U2's arrival in Berlin on the day of German reunification, including their initial booking at Hansa Studios and Bono's unusual housing experience, marked the strange beginning of the journey that led to the creation of the "Achtung Baby" album. "That was the strange start to the journey that would eventually result in the Oktung Baby album."
